limited_overlap.description: 968 of 12000 training applicants have a fitted enrolment probability below 0.02; their median prior earnings are 73,620 dollars. Their effects are extrapolated from the other applicants.
199 of 4000 new applicants have a fitted enrolment probability below 0.02; their predicted effects rest on extrapolation.

warnings: Follow-up survey response: 10073 of 12000 applicants answered (83.9%). Response depends on enrolment (logit coefficient 0.49 per enrolment). Results assume response is random given the covariates and enrolment; nothing in the data tests this, and response that depends on unobserved earnings would bias every estimate.
Final model: linear. RScorer (held-out responders): linear=-0.0020, causal_forest=-0.0002.

Instrument check: distance_km first-stage t statistic given covariates = -9.3; its direct t statistic in the follow-up earnings regression = 0.55. Distance-based IV estimate of the ATE = -7361 (90% -18496 to 3774).

Conditional-on-employment earnings effect = -445 (90% -1189 to 300); this compares employed applicants only, so it is not a causal effect on earnings of the employed unless employment is unaffected by enrolment.

Omitted-confounder benchmark: ATE when each strong confounder is dropped from the adjustment set: without prior_earnings = -7936, without months_unemployed = -83, without education = 61; full model = 203.
Run time 17 seconds with seed 1; training rows 12000, responders 10073.
